newsitem.title: QATAR: Sumitomo, Paribas to fund $650 mln Qatar petrochem.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo, Paribas to fund $650 mln Qatar petrochem.

text.p: Japan's Sumitomo Corp 8053.t and France's Paribas Bank will jointly arrange finance for most of a $650 million Qatari petrochemical project, industry officials said on Monday.

They will arrange commercial loans and export credits covering up to 70 percent of the cost of Qatar Fuel Additives Company (Qafac) project to set up a methanol and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) plant, the added.
The rest will be arranged by equity contribution from shareholders.
"Sumitomo and Paribas have agreed to arrange the finance for the project at the request of Japan's Chiyoda Corp ", an industry source said.
"The two giants have already started inviting other bankers and financial agencies to join the syndication", he added.

Qafac signed a $425 million engineering, procurement and construction contract with Chiyoda last Monday to build manufacturing and storage facilities for the project. Construction is expected to begin next month.
Qafac, one of the state's petrochemical projects, is 50 percent owned by the government's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) and the rest by three foreign partners.
Taiwan's state-run Chinese Petroleum Corporation holds 20 percent while Canada's International Octane Ltd and the private Lee Chang Yung Chemical Industry Corp of Taiwan each hold 15 percent.
The project, in Messeid 48 km (24 miles) off Doha, is expected to produce an annual 850,000 tonnes of methanol and 620,000 tonnes of environment-friendly MTBE from mid-1999.
The Taiwanese partners have already pledged to take a third of the output besides their equity stake in the project.
The project to use 100 million cubic feet per day of North Field gas and 500,000 tonnes per year of Butane, supplied by QGPC.
The Gulf Arab state has the third largest gas reserves in the world.
